title: Day 13 — Kill the Mutants (Test Strength)
prompt: Here's a correct median function and five subtly-broken versions of it. Your job isn't to fix code — it's to write checks strong enough to catch every broken version while still accepting the correct one. How do you pick your test inputs?

clarifications.answer: Five mutants: does-not-sort, returns-mean, even-upper (no average), odd-off-by-one, and empty-returns-zero.
One mutant returns the mean. You need an input where mean != median to catch it — a skewed distribution.
One mutant forgets to sort. Use an UNSORTED input whose median differs from the element at the middle index.
The correct function throws on empty input; one mutant returns 0. assert that median([]) throws.
Cover both: an odd-length list (catches odd-off-by-one) and an even-length list (catches even-upper and mean).
Only edit assertions.ts. spec.ts and check.test.ts are read-only.

hints: Go mutant by mutant: for each one, what is the smallest input where the correct median and that mutant DISAGREE?

[3,1,2] has median 2, but does-not-sort returns nums[1]=1 and odd-off-by-one returns sorted[mid-1]=1 — so both disagree. A skewed even list like [1,3,2,10] (median 2.5, mean 4, upper 3) catches mean and even-upper.
Three assertions suffice: median([3,1,2])===2, median([1,3,2,10])===2.5, and assert median([]) throws.
